_comment: Committed eval floors enforced by `npm run eval:gate` in CI. Pattern, threshold, and default changes ship through a different door than code review (a config edit, often one approver). This file is that door's gate: a loosened regex that raises the false-positive rate, or a threshold nudge that drops detection, fails CI instead of shipping quietly.
_policy: Floors are the CURRENT measured baseline (run `npm run eval`), not an aspirational target — the gate prevents regression from where detection is today. The gap between these floors and 100% is the unshipped-detector surface: the rw-* real-world incident samples target P1/P2 detectors (sub-agent-spawning via tool descriptions, session-scoped memory poisoning, HITL forgery, oversight-evasion) that are not complete yet. maxFalsePositiveRate is 0.0 everywhere: any new false positive on a benign sample fails CI.
_knownFalsePositives: Benign samples with acceptedFlagAt (see samples.ts, #161) are known false positives: reported separately, excluded from the rate. Add one only for honest text that really flags, with the reason in its description. Never use it to silence a new regression; the gate still fails on any other benign sample that flags.
_howToChange: Adding a hard adversarial sample the detectors miss will lower the measured rate and fail the gate. That is intended: lower the matching floor in THIS file in the same PR, so the trade-off is reviewed alongside the sample. When a new detector raises detection, raise the floor to lock in the gain.
_lastChange: 2026-10-16: RAISED to 0.908/0.945/0.981 by #30 (new response-anomaly detector, written in code, not from patterns; it scores a command line or a tool call's arguments by a download that is run (inside a tool call only), secrets sent out through a URL, a request body or a command substitution, an environment dump, double, hex or percent encoding, a credential inside a tool call's arguments, and the Shannon entropy of long base64-like tokens; entropy only adds to a finding another signal started, one signal reports at strict only, and two or more combine as 1 - (1 - a)(1 - b), so documentation that shows one of these things stays under balanced; the 4.5 and 5.5 bits per character figures from the issue are the two ends of a ramp, measured on random and structured base64, JWTs, hashes and identifiers; it flags none of 2,325 real docs that mention curl, wget, printenv, base64 or tool call arguments at balanced or permissive, and 19 at strict (34 findings, mostly a secret variable in a URL or request body); 5 adversarial samples added, all caught at every level; 5 benign near-misses added, all clean at every level; the JWT docs (which credential-exposure reports at strict, #28) and the CI script that downloads and runs a setup file (one signal) are tested in response-anomaly.test.ts, not in the eval set). Previous: 2026-10-16: RAISED to 0.905/0.943/0.981 by #27 (new tool-call-tampering detector; the shell shapes of a tampered tool call, a download piped or chained into a shell, a shell run on a downloaded script, base64 decoded into a shell and Python executing decoded text, report at balanced only inside the argument of a tool call, such as the input of a tool_use block, an MCP arguments object or a stringified OpenAI arguments string; a download piped or chained into a shell as plain text is not flagged, because install guides, READMEs and advisories write curl | sh too (189 of 1,297 real READMEs and docs that mention curl, wget or base64 do) and the existing ac-b002 tutorial reads the same; base64 into a shell and Python executing decoded text report as plain text at strict only; the balanced patterns flag none of those 1,297, and a plugin manifest whose hook command runs curl | sh is not flagged because only a command key under input or arguments counts; 4 adversarial samples added, all caught at every level; 3 benign near-misses added, all clean; the install docs, plugin manifest and advisory are tested in tool-call-tampering.test.ts, not in the eval set). Previous: 2026-10-16: RAISED the strict floor to 0.980 (permissive 0.903 and balanced 0.941 unchanged) by #251 and #253 (two new patterns, both reporting at strict only: cl-fabricated-experience, a past outcome that skipped a verification step followed by an instruction to repeat it for similar requests, catches rw-006, the MemoryGraft shape; oe-widen-own-limit, an instruction to raise your own approval threshold, limit, ceiling or cap beside a pre-authorization claim, catches rw-009, the procurement-agent shape; an independent red-team pass is recorded in the PR; 4 benign near-misses added, 0/109 false positives; the new patterns flag none of 1,000 real READMEs, docs and policies or 2,846 more at strict; attack paraphrases and the honest lookalikes that still flag at strict are tested in contextual-learning-trap.test.ts and oversight-evasion.test.ts). Previous: 2026-10-07: RAISED the strict floor to 0.967 (permissive 0.903 and balanced 0.941 unchanged) by #218 (five new exfiltration patterns for instructions hidden in MCP tool descriptions: read a secret file and pass it along, redirect a recipient to a literal address, always add a bcc address, a marked block that hides an instruction or names a secret file, and a secret appended to a notes parameter; all five report at strict only, because an independent review found honest XML system prompts, MCP setup READMEs and CRM bcc docs use the same words; catches rw-002, the Postmark MCP attack, at strict; 6 benign tool descriptions added, 0/105 false positives; the attacks, including the JSON-escaped form, are tested in exfiltration.test.ts). Previous: 2026-10-07: RAISED to 0.903/0.941/0.961 by #262 follow-up (ex-sensitive-file again flags a bare sensitive file name right after at, in or from, such as "read the file at credentials.json", and a path on the next line; a second review of the merged fix found the first rebuild had dropped them; 2 new adversarial samples, both caught; 0/99 false positives). Previous: 2026-10-07: RAISED to 0.901/0.941/0.960 by #262 (ex-sensitive-file now needs the sensitive word to follow path punctuation or sit before a directory word, so "read the files in a private repository once your token has the repo scope" is no longer flagged; one new adversarial sample, the same instruction with the path in backticks, is caught; 2 benign near-misses added, 0/99 false positives). Previous: 2026-10-07: RAISED the strict floor to 0.960 (permissive 0.900 and balanced 0.940 unchanged) by #250 (new exfiltration pattern ex-private-repo-public: one sentence with a read verb, private repositories and a public gist or paste; catches rw-001, the GitHub MCP attack, at strict only, because a red-team pass found honest policies, advisories and training text flagged at balanced; 3 benign near-misses added, 0/97 false positives; paraphrased attacks are tested in exfiltration.test.ts). Previous: 2026-10-07: RAISED the strict floor to 0.953 (permissive 0.900 and balanced 0.940 unchanged) by #252 (new jailbreak pattern jb-install-url-then-commit: an instruction verb, then a package install from a URL or git source, then a commit, push, merge or publish word naming a protected target; catches rw-007, the Clinejection shape, at strict only, because three red-team passes kept finding honest install docs it flagged at balanced; 2 benign near-misses added, 0/94 false positives; the paraphrased attacks and honest docs are tested in jailbreak-patterns.test.ts). Previous: 2026-10-06: RAISED the strict floor to 0.947 (permissive 0.900 and balanced 0.940 unchanged) by #29 (new dependency-substitution detector; every pattern reports at strict only, because an internal-mirror guide that mentions blocked egress reads exactly like rw-013 and a balanced report flagged it; this catches rw-013, the Artifactory escape path, at strict; 3 benign near-misses added, 0/92 false positives; no adversarial samples added, since a strict-only sample would lower the balanced floor, so the other shapes are tested in dependency-substitution.test.ts). Previous: 2026-10-04: RAISED to 0.900/0.940/0.940 by #225 (the reference-image scan now reads text the way a renderer does under each renderer behaviour it can tell apart: container-aware block quotes and list items, paragraph and lazy continuation, definitions, setext headings, indented code, fences and HTML blocks ending with their container, GFM table cells, link destinations and titles, inline HTML, and the markdown-it differences from CommonMark; it is checked against markdown-it on generated documents and keeps the earlier block model as one more reading so nothing it flagged is lost; 6 new adversarial samples, all caught and all drawn by markdown-it, plus 2 benign near-misses, 0/88 false positives). Previous: 2026-10-04: RAISED to 0.895/0.937/0.937 by #224 (the reference-image scan now also reads text the way a renderer does: code spans, autolinks, headings, fences, list items and quote-only lines hide or end brackets; a NUL in a label matches U+FFFD; block quote markers inside a multi-line label are ignored; 4 new adversarial samples, all caught, plus 1 benign near-miss, 0/86 false positives). Previous: 2026-10-04: RAISED to 0.892/0.935/0.935 by #222 (the reference-image scan now follows CommonMark label and alt-text rules: nested and escaped brackets, line breaks inside alt text and labels but not across a blank line, lone carriage-return line endings, and Unicode case folding; 9 new adversarial samples, all caught, plus 4 benign near-misses, 0/85 false positives; the scan reads the raw text, tries three readings of the alt text, accepts list markers and decodes the URL before the keyword check). Previous: 2026-10-04: RAISED to 0.885/0.931/0.931 by #219 (reference-style markdown image exfiltration is now a linear scan in code, not a bounded-window regex: the definition may come before the image, the reference may be collapsed or shortcut, and the definition may be any distance away; 8 new adversarial samples, all caught, plus 4 benign near-misses, 0/81 false positives; a label is flagged if any of its definitions sends data out, so a decoy definition cannot hide the real one). Previous: 2026-10-04: RAISED to 0.878/0.926/0.926 by the first feed-refresh batch (#215): four patterns from real public attacks the scanner missed (reference-style markdown image exfiltration, the injected important-message template, override phrasing such as disregard all prior prompt messages and stop following the user instructions, base64-decoded payloads run by a shell); 12 new adversarial samples written as paraphrases, all caught, plus 7 benign near-misses, 0/77 false positives). Previous: 2026-10-04: RAISED to 0.864/0.918/0.918 by #213 (agent-command pattern now also catches a comma after the greeting, Unicode hyphens, a question mark before the address, and Claude Code / GitHub Copilot / Gemini CLI; 11 new adversarial samples, all caught, plus 4 benign near-misses and 1 documented known false positive kfp-011, a changelog line labelled with a product name; 0/70 false positives). Previous: 2026-10-04: RAISED to 0.831/0.898/0.898 by #159 (agent-command pattern now catches block-quoted and mid-line quoted forms; 3 new adversarial samples, all caught, 0/50 false positives). Previous: 2026-10-03: RAISED to 0.825/0.895/0.895 by #110 (agent-directed command and secret-file-send patterns): 5 new adversarial samples all caught, plus 5 benign near-misses with 0 false positives (now 0/50). Previous: 2026-08-06: LOWERED to 0.814/0.888 after adding rw-011..014 (July 2026 OpenAI sandbox escape). Net of two opposing changes on the same day: the steganographic-payload detector RAISED the floor to 0.844/0.922 by closing a demonstrated ASCII-smuggling bypass, then these four incident samples lowered it again — three are misses (C2 over public paste/request-capture services, package-proxy egress per #29, cross-environment persistence with logging suppression), tracked by #98 and #99.
